usability_test.objective: Decide whether the extract-verify-review chain can be trusted end to end before build: whether an associate will commit machine-extracted terms without re-keying them, and whether a reviewer will accept a figure on provenance alone rather than reopening the agreement. If either answer is no, the time savings the business case rests on do not exist, whatever the rest of the design does.

participants.recruit_from: Four associates and three reviewers from mid-market credit desks who build profiles by hand today, plus two MDs with booked-portfolio responsibility. Recruited through the two desks that took part in discovery, excluding the eleven already interviewed so the design is not tested on the people who described the problem.

tasks.scenario: You've picked up a new borrower this morning and the credit committee meets Thursday. Get as far as you can toward being ready.
tasks.success_criteria: Participant establishes what the firm already knows about the entity before starting original work, unaided, and can say afterwards what the blocking input was without being prompted.
probes: Match between system and the real world

tasks.scenario: Here is the credit agreement for that borrower. You need the covenant package and the leverage definitions in a state you'd be willing to put your name to.
tasks.success_criteria: Participant commits terms rather than re-keying them, and when asked which figures they checked individually, names the low-confidence ones rather than 'all of them' or 'none'. Time to commit recorded against the four-to-five-hour baseline.

tasks.scenario: Two of the documents in that set define EBITDA differently. Get the profile to a state you'd submit.
tasks.success_criteria: Participant notices the conflict without being told it exists, and resolves it deliberately rather than by accepting whichever value the interface offered first.

tasks.scenario: You're reviewing this profile. Decide whether you'd sign it off.
tasks.journey_stage: Risk review and verification (Credit Risk Reviewer)
tasks.success_criteria: Participant verifies at least three figures via provenance rather than opening the source agreement, and reaches a sign-off decision inside ten minutes against the twenty-to-thirty-minute baseline.

tasks.scenario: Sign this profile off. Then: you've realised you signed the wrong one.
tasks.journey_stage: Risk review and verification (Credit Risk Reviewer)
tasks.success_criteria: Participant recovers without assistance and without contacting an administrator. Whether they noticed the confirmation before confirming is recorded separately — a confirmation people click through is not a safeguard.

tasks.scenario: A figure on this review can't be traced to a source clause. Do what you'd normally do.
tasks.journey_stage: Defect return and rework loop (Reviewer and Associate)
tasks.success_criteria: Participant returns the defect against the specific figure rather than as a general comment, and does not attempt to sign off around it.
probes: Help users recognize, diagnose and recover from errors

tasks.scenario: It's Monday morning and you have twenty minutes before your first meeting. Tell me what in the portfolio needs you this week.
tasks.success_criteria: Participant acts on or dismisses each attention item from the feed entry alone, and correctly states whether the scores they acted on were current — the stale-score case is included in the fixture data.

usability_test.what_would_change_the_design: If associates in T2 re-key rather than commit, extraction confidence is not doing its job and the reconciliation UI on 03 is rebuilt before build starts — the feature's whole premise fails, not a detail of it. If reviewers in T4 reopen the agreement instead of using provenance, the click-to-source treatment on 04/06 is redesigned and the review-time target is withdrawn from the business case rather than quietly missed. If two or more participants in T5 confirm sign-off without reading the dialog, the 10-minute reversal window becomes the primary safeguard and the dialog is demoted, because a confirmation people click through is decoration. If T7 participants act on stale scores believing them current, the staleness treatment on 07 is escalated from a banner to a blocking state.

metric_plan.metric: Hours from receiving the agreement set to a committed term sheet
metric_plan.baseline_source: Stage-2 journey stage 3 — four to five hours of day one, from associate interviews
metric_plan.read_after: 20 committed agreements, roughly six weeks at current deal flow

metric_plan.metric: Hours to a verified corporate structure and guarantee package
metric_plan.baseline_source: Stage-2 journey stage 3 — the same four-to-five-hour figure, which is org-chart time specifically
metric_plan.read_after: 20 derived structures; manual_edits per structure is the honest read, not derivation count

metric_plan.metric: Minutes per risk review spent reopening source documents to verify a figure
metric_plan.baseline_source: Stage-2 journey stage 5 — twenty to thirty minutes per review, from the reviewer interview

metric_plan.metric: Lead time between a deterioration signal and it reaching the MD
metric_plan.baseline_source: Stage-2 journey stage 7 — signals surfacing roughly three months late, from the MD interview. Read from the scoring pipeline's own signal-to-surface log, not from a UI event: the metric is about when the system knew, not when someone looked.
metric_plan.read_after: Two quarters — the baseline is a three-month lag, so a shorter window cannot show movement

metric_plan.metric: Share of profile model fields re-keyed by hand from a PDF
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown — no current system records how much of a model is re-keyed; the fields_rekeyed_by_hand property establishes it from first use

metric_plan.metric: Share of questionable add-backs raised at review rather than after close
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown — today these are caught inconsistently and nothing records the misses; needs a retrospective read of post-close findings to establish
metric_plan.read_after: One quarter, and only alongside the post-close review that supplies the denominator

metric_plan.metric: Round trips to close a returned defect
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown — the current loop runs over email and is not countable; first 20 threads establish it

metric_plan.metric: Share of targets where prior firm contact is surfaced before manual hunting begins
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown. Not instrumented at launch: the metric needs an event on 02 that Stage 5 did not specify, because 02 is a read page and the instrumentation rule only floors write pages. Add precedent_surfaced before build.
metric_plan.read_after: Not readable until that event exists — tracked in open_baselines rather than assumed

metric_plan.metric: Share of firm precedent reachable by search rather than by asking a colleague
metric_plan.baseline_source: Index coverage report from the ingestion service — a backend figure, not a UI event; the denominator is the store inventory taken during discovery
metric_plan.read_after: First full index pass, then monthly

metric_plan.metric: Deal-clock days lost waiting on an unowned outstanding request
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown — deal-clock days lost to unowned requests is not recorded anywhere today; the tracker's own ageing report establishes it from first use

metric_plan.metric: Share of alerts acted on without opening another system to decide
metric_plan.baseline_source: unknown. Same gap as the precedent timeline: 07 and 08 are read-and-acknowledge pages, so Stage 5 specified no events for them. Acknowledge and escalate both need instrumenting before this is readable.
metric_plan.read_after: Not readable until those events exist

open_baselines: Share of targets where prior firm contact is surfaced before manual hunting begins — needs a precedent_surfaced event on 02, absent from Stage 5. Owner: the delivery stage, before build.
Share of firm precedent reachable by search rather than by asking a colleague — needs the store inventory from discovery turned into a denominator. Owner: platform, at first index pass.
Share of profile model fields re-keyed by hand from a PDF — establishes itself from the fields_rekeyed_by_hand property on first use; no retrospective read possible.
Share of questionable add-backs raised at review rather than after close — needs a retrospective read of post-close findings to supply the denominator. Owner: credit risk, one quarter.
Deal-clock days lost waiting on an unowned outstanding request — not recorded anywhere today; the tracker establishes its own baseline from first use.
Round trips to close a returned defect — the current email loop is not countable; first 20 threads establish it.
Share of alerts acted on without opening another system to decide — needs acknowledge and escalate events on 07/08, absent from Stage 5. Owner: the delivery stage, before build.
